subtitle: The Vedic litany to Rudra — the Namakam and the Camakam

text.en: Transcribed from the Veda Union Śrī Rudram (IAST, v1.6). The recitation marks are the owner's own: holdings, svara, the Taittirīya gum, the visarga forms, svarabhakti and the pauses are carried as data, not redrawn.
The nyāsa sections are marked with conventional (“artificial”) svaras, as the source says — they are not attested saṁhitā accents.

translation.en: Oṁ, from the lower depths to the sky, to the ends of the earth, throughout all worlds, and the vast shimmering universe. The radiant crystal Śiva-liṅga, gleaming at the crown, exuding the nectar of the full moon. Of aboundingly sanctified One Lord, always reciting the hymns of Rudra, one should meditate for the attainment of the desired high status, and may the wise one sprinkle Śiva (perform Abhiṣekam). DV

Pervades the whole Universe, the body resembling the Moon (himarucā) shining, with serpents, dark-throated, with matted locks, furnished with the crescent moon, and fierce bow in His hands. The three-eyed ones, adorned with Rudrākṣa garlands, manifesting powers and taking various forms of Śambhu, The Rudras that the Śrī Rudra hymn, reveals their powers, may they grant us happiness. DV

sections.title: Prathamo'nuvākaḥ
sections.source: kṛṣṇayajurveda · Taittirīya Saṁhitā 4.5 — the fifth prapāṭhaka of the fourth (Vaiśvadeva) kāṇḍa

translation.en: Salutations to the blessed Rudra.
Salutation to the Rudra’s furies, and to your beloved arrow (action) salutation. Salutation to your bow (aim) and salutation to your both arms.
That your arrow which is the most auspicious and auspicious is your bow. And with that auspicious quiver of yours o Rudra you make us happy.
O Rudra, your body that is auspicious is not terrifying and not evil looking. With that most peaceful body of yours become visible to us, o Lord of the mountains.
O Dweller in the mountains, the arrow you bear in your hand for shooting, o auspicious protector of the mountain, please make it not intend to harm people or herds.
We salute you with auspicious words, o mountain lord, so that for us the whole world may indeed be healthy and friendly.
The protector and the first divine healer declared, that all snakes and all evil spirits are crushed.

text.en: in “jambhayant sarvāśca” the letter “t” is āgama, inserted letter, called abhinidhānaḥ (T. Pr. XIV. 9.)

translation.en: That one who is copper-red, reddish as the dawn, that is brown, and auspicious, All these Rudras who are situated around in the thousands directions, we beg protection from their wrath.
That blue-throated and very red one who sneaks, the cowherds saw and the water-bearers saw Him, and Him having been seen by all the creatures grants us happiness.
Salutation to the blue-throated thousand-eyed bountiful one, and also to all those beings of his, to them I offered my salutations.
You loosen the bow string from both of the tips, and those arrows in your hand, o blessed one, may you throw them away.
Having unstrung the bow, you are a thousand-eyed owner of a hundred quivers, and having broken off the arrow tips, be auspicious and benevolent to us!
Unstrung is the bow of him with the matted hair, and pointless is the arrow, his arrows are lost, empty is his quiver.
O most generous one the arrow that was in your hand, and your bow, You are that one with freedom from disease, please protect us from all sides!
May there be salutations to you, the courageous one and to the unstrung weapon, and salutation to both of your hands and to your bow.
May the arrow from your bow avoid us from all sides, Likewise that quiver of yours, please place it there far from us.
Salutations to Śambhu.

Salutations to the revered Lord of the Universe, to the great God, to the three-eyed one, annihilator of Tripura, to the one who embodies the three fires and time, to Rudra as the fire of time, to the blue-throated one, to the conqueror of death, to the Lord of all, to the eternally auspicious one (to Śaṅkara, the giver of peace), to to the glorious and great god, salutations!

translation.en: Salutation to the eldest and to the youngest. Salutations to the firstborn and to the later-born. Salutation to the one in the middle and to the next to the oldest one. Salutation to the latest one and to the next one. Salutations to the one in Gandharvas’ city of Sobha and to the one at an incantation.

Salutation to the one who belongs to Yama and to the one at peace. Salutations to the one of the fertile lands and to the one on the grains threshing floor. Salutations to the praiseworthy one and to the one whose name belongs in a verse. Salutations to the one in the woods and to the one in shrubs or dry grass. Salutations to the one who is sounding and to the one who echoes.

Salutation to the one with a helmet and to the one with a coat of mail. Salutations to the one renowned or famous and to the one leading renowned armies.

translation.en: Salutation to the one of a war drum and to the one beating the drum. Salutation to the courageous one and to the one who is seizing. Salutation to the envoy and to the dispatched one. Salutation to the one with a bow and to the quiver-holder.

Salutation to the one with sharp arrows and to the armed one. Salutations to the one with his own weapon and to the one with a good bow. Salutations to the one of the road and to the one of the pathway. Salutations to the one in a hole and to the one on the ground.

sections.title: Daśamo'nuvākaḥ
sections.source: kṛṣṇayajurveda · Taittirīya Saṁhitā 4.5 — the fifth prapāṭhaka of the fourth (Vaiśvadeva) kāṇḍa

translation.en: O Hastener, lord of soma, unattached blue-red (purple) one, don’t let these people and cattle fear, nor they die swiftly, but at some other time.
Your benevolent form is said to be auspicious for healing the world. With that Rudra’s auspicious remedy, grant us bliss for life.
To Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, who destroys enemy heroes, we offer devotion. May our peace be eternal, so every human and animal in this village is nourished and free from disease.
Be gracious to us, O Rudra, and bring us joy. To the destroyer of heroes, we offer our reverence. The peace and health won by our father Manu, may we obtain these under your able guidance, O Rudra.
Do not harm our elders, our children, those who are growing, and do not harm those who have grown. Do not kill our beloved father or mother, nor harm their bodies, O Rudra.
Do not harm our children, our descendants, our lifespan, our cows, or our horses. O Rudra, do not kill in anger our brave men who offer sacrifices. We worship you with reverence.
May your cow-killing and man-slaying be far away, O destroyer of heroes. Let your favor be with us. Protect us and speak over us, O god. Then grant us happiness, O two-fold exalted one.

Praise the renowned, chariot-seated, young one, fierce like a fearsome beast, who strikes down. Be gracious to the worshipper, O Rudra, who is praising you. Let the armies of others be destroyed for us.

May the weapon of Rudra be warded off from us, may the evil intention of the fierce one be away from harm. Protect the firm and generous ones, extend your bounty. Be gracious to our children and descendants.
O most bountiful and most auspicious one, be benevolent to us. Having placed your weapon on the highest tree, advance wearing the skin, come bearing the Pinaka bow.
Salutations to you, o caster of arrows, o fiery one, o Lord. May your thousand weapons destroy others, not us.
Thousands upon thousands are the weapons in your arms. O blessed Lord, make the faces of those (weapons) turned away.

sections.title: Ekādaśo'nuvākaḥ
sections.source: kṛṣṇayajurveda · Taittirīya Saṁhitā 4.5 — the fifth prapāṭhaka of the fourth (Vaiśvadeva) kāṇḍa

translation.en: Thousands upon thousands of Rudras who are on the earth, Their bows we unstring thousand yojanas away.
Also of the Rudras in this great ocean, and in the atmosphere,
(also) of blue-necked, white-throated Rudras, who move below the earth,
(also) of the blue-necked, white-throated Rudras, who have taken refuge in heaven,
(also) those in the trees who are yellowish like young grass, blue-necked, and reddish,
(also) those who are the uncrowned lords of beings, with matted hair,
(also) those in the food and drinking cups who are piercing people,
(also) those who are the protectors of the paths of the givers of food, and of the warriors eager to fight,
(also) the spear bearers and sword bearers who move about the sacred places,
(also) the Rudras who have spread in many many directions, their bows we unstring thousand yojanas away.

Salutation to the Rudras who are on the earth, in the atmosphere, and in heaven, whose food, and wind, and rain are the arrows, ten in the east, ten in the south, ten in the west, ten in the north, ten upward, salutation to them. May they be gracious to us. Those whom we hate and who hate us, I place them in your jaws.

sections.title: Śrīrudrapraśnasyopasaṁhāra
sections.source: kṛṣṇayajurveda · Taittirīya Saṁhitā 4.5 — the fifth prapāṭhaka of the fourth (Vaiśvadeva) kāṇḍa

translation.en: We worship the three-eyed one, who is fragrant and is nourishing all growth. Like breaking free from binding of a great affliction, may I be freed from death, but not from immortality!
Rudra who is in the fire, who is in the waters, who is in the plants, who has entered all the worlds, to that Rudra let us salute.
Praise him indeed, the archer with a good bow, who rules over all cures. For well-being we worship with reverence the god Rudra, the divine spirit of blessings giving.
This hand of mine is divine, this hand of mine is more divine. This hand of mine is the universal healer, this hand of mine has an auspicious touch.
Those myriads of nooses of yours, O Death, for killing mortals, by the power of the yajña we worship all of them for protection.
To Death, svāhā! To Death, svāhā!
Oṁ, salutations to the blessed one, to Rudra and to Viṣṇu. Protect me from death! You are the knot of the life forces, O Rudra, the destroyer of death, be nourished by that food!
Salutations to Rudra and to Viṣṇu. Protect me from death!
Always auspicious, Om
Om, peace, peace, peace

sections.source: kṛṣṇayajurveda · Taittirīya Saṁhitā 4.7 — the seventh prapāṭhaka of the fourth (Vaiśvadeva) kāṇḍa

translation.en: Earth goddess Iḍā calls upon the divine Bṛhaspati and the mankind engaged in sacrifice chanting praises, and all-gods recited the sacred hymns. You should not intend to harm mother Earth.
I shall think pleasant and I shall beget pleasant, I shall speak pleasant and I will utter pleasant,
Striving that the speech is endowed with sweetness for the gods to willingly obey the men, and this very me that the gods should favour for splendour. May the ancestors rejoice.
Peace, peace, peace.

Words so that the meaning may be altered]

translation.en: Oṁ, from the lower depths to the sky, to the ends of the earth, throughout all worlds, and the vast shimmering universe. The radiant crystal Śiva-liṅga, gleaming at the crown, exuding the nectar of the full moon. Of aboundingly sanctified One Lord, always reciting the hymns of Rudra, one should meditate for the attainment of the desired high status, and may the wise one sprinkle Śiva (perform Abhiṣekam). DV

Pervades the whole Universe, the body shining, resembling the Moon (himarucā), with serpents, dark-throated, with matted locks, furnished with the crescent moon, and fierce bow in His hands. The three-eyed ones, adorned with Rudrākṣa garlands, manifesting powers and taking various forms of Śambhu, The Rudras that the Śrī Rudra hymn, reveals their powers, may they grant us happiness. DV

text.en: The five offerings, the artificial svaras.

translation.en: laṁ, to the one whose essence is Earth (Pṛthivī), I mentally offer fragrance.

text.en: roll the thumbs over the little fingers

translation.en: haṁ, to the one whose essence is Ether (Ākāśa), I mentally offer flowers.

text.en: roll the index fingers over the thumbs

translation.en: yaṁ, to the one whose essence is Air (Vāyu), I mentally offer incense.

text.en: roll the thumbs over the index fingers

To Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, who destroys enemy heroes, we offer devotion. May our peace be eternal, so every human and animal in this village is nourished and free from disease.
I sin, my actions are sinful, my soul is sinful, and I'm born of sin. Protect me, o Lord of Pārvatī, be the remover of all sins.
I'm devoid of mantra, fail at Kriyā, and without devotion, o ever-auspicious one, but whatever prayers I do, o God, may you be content by my rendering as they are.
I don't know the invocation, neither the conclusion of the ritual, nor I know how to worship. Please forgive me o Supreme Lord!
Thousands of mistakes I do day and night, but because you know me as your servant, please forgive me o Supreme Lord!
You indeed are my shelter and otherwise the shelter does not exist. Therefore with the feeling of compassion, please forgive me o Supreme Lord.
